name: Vatnagedda
body:
VATNAGEDDA
CR 1

This small round-bodied flatfish has tiny eyes and fine hairs on its body. Its golden-yellow skin has a soft but unsettling sheen.

XP 400
N Tiny magical beast (aquatic)
Init +2; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +5

DEFENSE

AC 14, touch 14, flat-footed 12 (+2 Dex, +2 size)
hp 15 (2d10+4)
Fort +5, Ref +5, Will +1
Defensive Abilities corrosive toxic secretions
Weaknesses light blindness, light vulnerability

OFFENSE

Speed swim 30 ft.
Space 2 1/2 ft.; Reach 0 ft.
Special Attacks poison

STATISTICS

Str 4, Dex 15, Con 14, Int 1, Wis 12, Cha 9
Base Atk +2; CMB +2; CMD 9
Feats Ability Focus (poison)
Skills Perception +5, Swim +14
SQ protective gear

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Corrosive Toxic Secretions (Su)

The skin and flesh of the vatnagedda exude incredibly corrosive secretions. Any creature that strikes a vatnagedda with a natural attack or unarmed strike takes 2d4 points of acid damage if it fails a DC 13 Reflex save. A creature that strikes a vatnagedda with a melee weapon must make a DC 13 Reflex save or the weapon takes 2d4 points of acid damage. These corrosive secretions are extremely potent, dissolving both organic and inorganic matter alike, and ignore hardness of less than 20. These secretions are also fully effective against incorporeal creatures, similar to a ghost touch weapon.

Even after the creature’s death, it continues to exude these secretions for at least a week. If the vatnagedda remains in contact with a creature or object for a full round, this damage increases to 10 + 1/2 the vatnagedda’s HD + Con modifier of acid damage (13 points per round for a typical vatnagedda). A creature exposed to these secretions is also exposed to corrosive venom. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Light Vulnerability (Ex)

When exposed to bright light, a vatnagedda takes 1 hit point per HD of damage per round of exposure (2 damage per round for a typical vatnagedda).

Poison (Su)

Corrosive Venom—contact; save Fort DC 17*; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds*; effect 1d4 Con*; cure 3 consecutive saves.

A creature that fails 3 consecutive saves takes Con drain instead of Con damage. The save DC is Constitution-based and includes a +2 racial bonus.

* See protective measures below.

Protective Gear (Ex)

There are several effective methods to significantly reduce the danger from a vatnagedda’s corrosive toxins. Wearing gloves made from multiple layers of skate skin, or alternatively crafted from human skin, provide some protection but may still result in inflammation and rashes. Protected creatures handling a vatnagedda’s body must still make DC 13 Reflex saves to avoid exposure, but only take 1d4 acid damage on a failed save and the poison is reduced to: save Fort DC 15; frequency 1/round for 3 rounds; effect 1 Con; cure 3 consecutive saves.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold lakes
Organization solitary
Treasure none

The vatnagedda is renowned as one of the most toxically deadly species of fish. Despite its flounder-like appearance, the vatnagedda is also known as the “loch-pike” or eiturgedda (“poisonous pike”). This fish hates light and dwells at the bottom of murky lakes. Vatnageddas are about 1 foot in length and weigh between 10 and 20 pounds.

Catching a Vatnagedda

Why risk catching such a poisonous fish? Because even ghosts, haunts, and other malevolent spirits aren’t immune to the vatnagedda, and the presence of a dead specimen, usually buried under the threshold of a residence, is enough to drive them away. Additionally, vatnagedda fat is a cure for aliments caused by evil spirits or foul magics.

The first consideration should be researching the vatnagedda. To discover the information listed below requires DC 16 Diplomacy checks to gather information or DC 16 Knowledge (arcana) checks, and discovering everything may require several such checks. To have any chance of catching a vatnagedda, the hook must be baited with gold, usually a ring, worth at least 5 gp. These golden objects are easily digested and absorbed by the vatnagedda, making this a significant cost of fishing for one. Vatnageddas hate light and are only seen near the surface during thick fog, before a storm, or late at night. After baiting the hook, catching this fish requires three successful DC 15 Survival checks or DC 12 Profession (fisherman) checks. Throwing in a line from a boat in the middle of the lake has the best chance, as casting a line from shore increases the DC of these checks by 2. Failing two consecutive checks or failing a check by 5 or more means losing the bait and costs at least half an hour of time.

Once caught, the vatnagedda should be dispatched quickly by those wearing protective gear, before it burns a hole through the bottom of the boat. If tossed onto shore, the vatnagedda may eventually suffocate, but it’s flopping around is a potential hazard for those nearby. Also, the creature’s corrosive toxins are so powerful that it can melt its way through the ground and disappear into the earth.

The main challenge after landing a vatnagedda is holding on to it, as its secretions can eventually destroy almost any material placed around it. Placing the dead fish in a glass bottle, and then wrapping it with multiple layers of sheepskin, leather, and horse-skin does allow it to be transported. However, any creature carrying this bundle periodically risks exposure and when the dead vatnagedda dissolves its way through the bundle, moving it to a fresh carrying container is also an exposure risk. The only known way to safely transport a vatnagedda is to wrap it in the caul of a humanoid child and then the caul of a calf.

Extracting the valuable fat from the vatnagedda corpse requires a DC 13 Craft (alchemy) or Profession (butcher, cook, or fisherman) check. Each attempt risks exposure unless the creature has the poison use class feature and the acidic secretions are likely to ruin any tools used. A dose of vatnagedda fat acts like a restoration spell combined with cure critical wounds but only for ability damage, ability drain, hit point damage, and temporary or permanent negative levels caused by incorporeal undead, necromancy effects, or negative energy damage. A vatnagedda has enough fat for a single dose.
